Student progress intelligence

One place to see participation, learning progress, and advisor follow-up.

ⓘ
Demonstration only: 20 fictional students, generated app events and program activities. No production analytics or health/wearables. Anonymous aliases are not real student records.

Daily focus — trend

Completed focus minutes across selected students · not passive app-open time

App sessions
Minutes per active student per day

Three-lens scorecard

Distinct signals, not an opaque combined score

Daily habits

Average participating student, selected period

Immediate attention

Flagged cases for an advisor's human review

Review only

Chapter readiness by subject

Latest achieved evidence stage as of selected end date

Five-stage academic rigor

Strict ordinal progression; higher stage requires preceding steps

1 Read
2 Notes
3 Practice ≥70%
4 Timed paper
5 Readiness ≥80%
A chapter isn't marked exam-ready because notes are complete. Advisors check process adherence and evidence; subject-specific tutoring is escalated to qualified educators.

Student academic overview

Aggregated stage progression and last update date, no grades displayed as medical or behavioral labels

Activities and delivery assurance

Planned vs held, attendance and optional usefulness ratings

Monthly / quarterly milestones

Deadline adherence and roadmap completion for the selected students

Career, personal, academic and social impact milestones are separate categories. Completion is based on an advisor-confirmed action, not the duration a student remained inside the app.

Prioritized action queue

Transparent, evidence-based prompts for human review; never automatic messages to minors

Demo rules

Exception criteria and data quality

Proposed SLAs; must be validated with Alcovia's advisors

Stalled chapter: no chapter-stage evidence in the last 14 days. Quiz participation: fewer than 2 attempts in the last 7 days. Overdue milestones: past-due roadmap items without advisor-confirmed completion. Missing task plans: no timetable plans for the past 3 school days. Advisors should check context, exam calendars and holiday schedules before contacting anyone.
